author: Confused_AFC
text_post: I broke the cardinal rule! Hey Guys, Maybe you all can help. Gf and I have been together for 3 years. Back in May we had a fight and we broke up, and she spent a few nights at her mom's house in a faraway city and came back. We reconciled and all was fine. Well we ended up moving to that faraway city a week ago. She then dumped me the other day for silly reasons and I moved out. I was pretty sad but shit happens. I maintained communication and went out this weekend to try to get back in the swing of things. Well I broke the cardinal rule this morning. I looked in her email. She emailed a guy (she always told me he was gay) saying how she always loved him and blah blah blah, but she referenced the time when she went to the faraway city alone, and apparently she drove by his work and he wouldn't see her. She also said how it's pathetic that she's still writing him and that she has to move on with her life. Yes, I was wrong to look in her email. My gut knew something was fishy. Well now she wants to get back together. I initiated the get-back by using the same language she used in the email to him... trying to spark some White Knight Syndrome in her, maybe. It worked. She says she hasn't slept with anyone since I left, and I asked if she dumped me to be with any "old flames." She says no. It sounds like she tries to get with this guy when we have issues. It also sounds like he has rejected her in some way. It reminds me of Friends (remember "We were on a break!"). I'd love to continue getting back with her, and while I think she was faithful during our times together, I'm concerned about all this hidden emotion... but because I snooped, I can't just talk it through with her. Any thoughts?

author: Hrang
text_post: Any mutual trust in your relationship is fubar. Are you planning on telling her what you did, which means revealing her secret as well? Lying is one of the more or less universal deal breakers. Why do you still want to be the girl? Do you think this train wreck is salvageable?

author: Confused_AFC
text_post: Thanks for the reply. Agreed about the trust problem. If the tables were turned though, I'd have probably told the same lie, so it's difficult for me to condemn. The question I ask myself is: which of us is the backup? Me because she got back with me when he never replied to the email... Or him because she only goes to him when we are broken up?

author: jiGsawyouth
text_post: I'd break it off dude. Any dishonesty in a relationship is grounds for a breakup in my opinion. Why would you want drama and trust issues?
